skill.name: set-up-magento-google-ads-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up Google Ads bidding on repeat purchases from Magento or Adobe Commerce. Check order classification and choose revenue or profit as the value for a retention campaign.
skill.summary: Set up and verify Google Ads bidding on Magento repeat purchases with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most scanner hits are documentation or scoped account lookups, not shell substitution or system reconnaissance. The installation steps introduce third-party code and dependency sources that require verification. The workflow lacks safeguards for setup writes, credential handling, and browser links; no evidence of deliberate exfiltration or audit-targeted prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Install commands rely on external code and package sources.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer and source revision. Verify module provenance and integrity, restrict the Composer repository to Product Metrics packages, and require a developer to test installation in staging.

remediation.issue: Setup writes lack a separate approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Before enabling tracking or creating actions, confirm the store view, destination account, data to be sent, and consent settings. Keep every unapproved channel disabled.

remediation.issue: Generic instructions allow collecting credentials unrelated to this skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exceptions from this Google Ads workflow. Use provider authorization pages or a managed secret store instead of chat or command arguments.

remediation.issue: The workflow forwards browser links from service responses without explicit validation.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the HTTPS origin and expected destination before showing a link. On failure, have the user navigate directly to the verified provider app.

semantic_findings.title: Setup writes lack explicit approval
semantic_findings.description: The workflow directs the agent to set up missing tracking without separately confirming the store view, account, or destination. Secondary actions can still receive order data after tracking starts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow reserves primary goals and browser actions for the user but gives no equivalent approval rule for authenticated setup writes. Actual writes depend on access.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule explicitly permits these exceptions and direct command use. It prohibits logging in prose but does not specify a secure input or runtime redaction mechanism.

content.user_title: Set Up Magento Returning Customer Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: Standard purchase goals do not distinguish repeat orders from first purchases. Use Product Metrics to verify repeat-order signals and choose a revenue or profit goal for your retention campaign.
actual_capabilities: Checks Product Metrics setup status for the selected company and property.
Reads whether recent orders in one store view count as new, returning, or unknown.
Guides setup and verification of the returning customer revenue and profit conversion actions.
Explains how to choose a conversion value and set a target ROAS for a retention campaign.
Reads back conversion action status after the merchant changes the campaign goal.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics and a developer-installed Magento module with cron running.
A person must authorize connections and make campaign bidding changes in Google Ads.
Returning customer history is limited to the same Magento store view.
Profit values depend on complete order costs and configured additional costs. Consent settings affect which orders reach Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Check setup readiness
use_cases.description: Find out whether your store view and Google Ads account are connected before planning a repeat-purchase campaign.

use_cases.title: Choose a retention campaign goal
use_cases.description: Compare repeat-order revenue and profit signals before selecting a goal for one retention campaign.

use_cases.title: Verify a repeat purchase event
use_cases.description: Check whether a paid test order arrived and was classified as returning after Magento cron ran.

prompt_templates.title: Check prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need before setting up Magento returning customer bidding in Google Ads? Explain what my developer and I each need to do.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are planning the setup and have not connected your store yet.

prompt_templates.title: Review recent orders
prompt_templates.prompt: Count how many of the last 20 paid orders in my selected store view were new, returning, or unknown. Do not show customer details.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to validate the repeat-order signal before using it for bidding.

prompt_templates.title: Compare revenue and profit
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether the returning customer revenue and profit actions are ready. Explain which value fits my retention campaign, and do not change any settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Your tracking is active and you are deciding which conversion value to use.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a pilot campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that my paid repeat test order arrived in the selected store view. Check the pilot campaign's goal, bid strategy, and target ROAS. Report mismatches without making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have set the campaign goal and want to verify the first test.

output_examples.input: Check whether my Magento store is ready to test returning customer bidding.
output: The Magento store view is active and linked to the selected property.
Google Ads is connected, but the returning customer conversion actions are not ready.
Verify the consent settings and review the conversion actions in Product Metrics before placing a test order.

output_examples.input: What should I check before using profit for my retention campaign?
output: Confirm that Magento provides product costs and that additional costs are active in Product Metrics.
Use Product Metrics - Returning Customer Profit as the pilot campaign goal.
Keep other campaigns on their current goals and verify the pilot goal after you save it.

output_examples.input: Why did my repeat customer's test order appear as new?
output_examples.output: The earlier order was in another store view. Product Metrics checks earlier paid orders only in the same view, using the customer account or guest email.

best_practices: Confirm the store view, Google Ads account, and consent settings before enabling tracking or creating conversion actions.
Validate a second paid test order in the same store view before using repeat-order conversions for bidding.
Pilot one retention campaign with its own goal and verify the action after saving.
anti_patterns: Do not use account-wide goals when only one retention campaign should bid on repeat orders.
Do not bid on profit before checking product costs and activating additional costs.
Do not share the Magento private configuration file or account credentials in chat.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics connects the Magento store view, classifies paid orders, and sends returning customer conversions to Google Ads.

faq.question: Can I install the Magento module from Magento Admin?
faq.answer: No. A developer installs the module on the server. On Magento 2.4, you can import the private configuration in Magento Admin after installation.

faq.question: When is a customer counted as returning?
faq.answer: The same account or guest email must have an earlier paid order in the same store view. Cancelled orders do not count.

faq.question: Is a conversion sent once per customer?
faq.answer: No. The integration sends a returning customer conversion for each qualifying paid repeat order, subject to consent.

faq.question: Why is the returning customer profit action empty?
faq.answer: Check that additional costs are active and that the order has complete cost data. Also check that the order was classified as returning.

faq.question: Can the assistant change which goal my campaign bids on?
faq.answer: No. You choose the goal in Google Ads. The assistant can read back the conversion action status after you make the change.
